correctness.rationale: The proof gives normalized open-path eigenvectors, an all-prime cyclotomic-independence argument that classifies every energy degeneracy, an invariant bright/dark split valid for all positive hopping and absorption rates, and the exact projector identity P_b=P_+-P_{0,+}+P_{0,w}. A finite sine fourth-moment and the (4I-A^2)/(2p) zero-band kernel give each of five site values and their multiplicities. Boundary cases p=3 and p=5, strictly positive loss, infinite time and scope were checked. Standalone finite spectral grouping matched all 1,364 sites over eight prime sizes (maximum error 2.78e-15); direct dissipative propagation reproduced three small cases. Finite computation is not substituted for the arbitrary-prime proof.

originality.rationale: The novel assessed statement is the complete site-resolved five-class probability formula and its two-corner full-capture criterion, not the already available trace/bright-space dimension. Material examination of the closest works finds general methods, random-lattice boundary absorption, and other graph families, but not the prime-grid local law. Prior scalar trace and rank statements do not logically determine the full diagonal of the capture projector. The cyclotomic decomposition plus zero-band rank-one projector and a localized (4I-A^2) kernel make an additional substantive calculation. Priority remains provisional, subject to specialized literature.

value.rationale: The physically natural initial-condition-dependent absorption probability is fully classified for every site on an infinite family of finite square quantum networks. A scalar average cannot select high-efficiency launch sites or predict the local separation-two anomaly. The exact full-capture opposite corner, four partial values, their labelled multiplicities and an all-site law make the result a concrete transport benchmark; the motive is not an arbitrarily selected finite graph or a tiny numerical refinement. It excludes the previously known mixed-state average and bright dimension as original.
